as_told.title: John Burke measures positive surface charge at stone circles

plain: Researchers are said to have measured energy fields at ancient pyramids and stone sites in Mexico and Central America, Europe and Egypt, and found that seeds kept there grew far better. Jim Weiner, a researcher of such sites, says from a book he calls Seeds of Knowledge, Stones of Power that they found "they increase yield per acre like three to five times." The pyramid researcher Geoffrey Drumm credits the same work to John Burke and his book, which he calls Seed of Knowledge, Stone of Plenty. Drumm says the fields were recorded with electrostatic voltmeters, instruments that measure static electric charge, and that they showed a positive charge on the ground at stone circles. He also names the researcher Hugh Newman. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would mean these ancient sites were built to do something practical, such as boost farming.
